title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its node values grouped by level, from left to right, top to bottom.
realWorld: Rendering a hierarchy one depth at a time — an org chart, a comment thread, a category menu — or serialising a tree for transport in a format that preserves shape.

bruteForce.idea: Compute the height, then for each depth re-walk the tree collecting only the nodes at that depth.
code: collectAtDepth(root, depth, level);   // re-walks from the root every time
private static void collectAtDepth(TreeNode node, int depth, List<Integer> into) {

complexity.time: O(n * h) — up to O(n^2) for a skewed tree

bruteForce.whySlow: Each level re-traverses everything above it. The root is visited h times, its children h-1 times, and so on.

patternIdentification: 'Level by level' is breadth-first search by definition. The refinement that makes it produce grouped output is freezing the queue size before each level.

optimized.idea: BFS with a queue. Capture queue.size() before the inner loop — that is exactly the number of nodes at the current depth, so one inner loop drains precisely one level.
code: int levelSize = queue.size();          // freeze BEFORE adding children

complexity.space: O(w) where w is the widest level — up to n/2

commonMistakes: Not freezing queue.size(), so levels bleed into one another.
Enqueueing null children, then null-checking on dequeue — it works but wastes queue space and invites NPEs.
Using ArrayList.remove(0) as a queue, which is O(n) per removal and turns this into O(n^2).
